meta.title: Main Course Pillar Pages — Content, SEO, Internal Linking & University Directory
meta.scope: Main course hub/pillar pages. This phase does NOT replace university-course pages or comparison pages.
meta.primary_goal: Make each main course page the authoritative informational hub that answers broad course intent and distributes authority to the exact university-course pages.

important_architecture.pillar: Main course page answers broad intent: what, eligibility, fees concept, syllabus, specialisations, admission, exams, career and how to compare.
important_architecture.cluster: University-course pages answer exact programme intent: University + course + current fees + eligibility + curriculum + admission + exam + electives.
important_architecture.comparison: Comparison pages answer decision intent between universities/programmes.
important_architecture.blog: Blogs answer narrow informational/search questions and should link upward to the relevant pillar and exact programme page.
important_architecture.rule: Do not make the pillar page compete with its own university-course pages for exact university + course queries.

Online MBA vs regular MBA vs distance MBA

opening.purpose: Immediately explain the course and what the page helps the learner decide.
opening.rule: Do not start with a generic marketing paragraph. Give a concise definition, target learner, major decision factors and a visible table of contents.

quick_facts.rule: Do not publish a single universal fee or eligibility value when universities differ.

fee_section.content: Explain how online-course fees differ by university, semester, one-time charges, examination/project charges and scholarships. Link every university's exact current fee to its university-course page.
fee_section.rule: Never present an invented 'average fee' as fact. If an estimate is useful, clearly label it as an editorial range and show methodology.

curriculum_section.content: Explain common curriculum areas at a high level, then link to university-specific semester curriculum pages. Specialisation content must identify the difference between core subjects and electives.
curriculum_section.rule: The pillar can explain curriculum patterns but must not pretend one generic syllabus applies to all universities.

factors: learner reviews only when independently sourced
comparison_framework.rule: Teach the user how to compare rather than declaring a university 'best' without a transparent methodology.

career_section.rule: Use role families and skill requirements. Avoid guaranteed placement, salary or promotion claims.

faq.rule: Only include questions genuinely answered by visible content. Do not generate hundreds of keyword variants.

university_directory_contract.purpose: Turn the pillar into a clean gateway to all 14 universities without creating thin duplicate content.
university_directory_contract.mobile: One card per row is acceptable in the directory; the flagship comparison component must remain separate and optimized for side-by-side decision making.
university_directory_contract.desktop: Use a clean grid/table hybrid where useful, but preserve the same information hierarchy.
university_directory_contract.links: Every card must deep-link to the exact canonical university-course page.
university_directory_contract.noindex: Do not create indexable filter combinations or parameter-generated university/course duplicates.

internal_linking.pillar_to_course: Every university card links to the exact university-course URL.
internal_linking.course_to_pillar: Every university-course page links back to its parent course hub.
internal_linking.pillar_to_comparison: Link to the relevant course comparison page.
internal_linking.pillar_to_blogs: Link only to high-value supporting articles.
internal_linking.blogs_to_pillar: Every relevant blog should have a contextual link to the pillar.
internal_linking.anchor_strategy: Use natural descriptive anchors; avoid repeating one exact-match anchor unnaturally.
internal_linking.section_anchors: Use #eligibility, #fees, #curriculum, #specialisations, #admission, #exams, #careers, #universities, #faqs where appropriate. Do not create separate indexable URLs for each anchor.

seo_contract.title_pattern: Online {COURSE} — Fees, Eligibility, Syllabus, Admission & Universities 2026-27 | CollegeSathi
seo_contract.h1: Online {COURSE}: Fees, Eligibility, Syllabus, Admission & Universities
seo_contract.meta_pattern: Compare Online {COURSE} options for 2026-27. Check eligibility, fees, syllabus, specialisations, admission, exams, careers and universities.
schema: FAQPage only when FAQs are visible and valid
ItemList for visible university directory where technically appropriate
seo_contract.eeat: Display last verified date and official-source links for dynamic facts.
seo_contract.year_rule: Do not create separate 2025/2026/2027 pages for the same evergreen course intent unless there is a genuine editorial reason. Update the canonical pillar and archive only when necessary.

search_intent_map.rule: Use these intents to structure content, not to create thin pages for every keyword.

content_quality.originality: Write original explanations and decision frameworks. Do not rewrite CollegeVidya, CollegeSathi, LearningRoutes or other competitor text.
content_quality.evidence: Dynamic claims must cite official university/regulator documents.
content_quality.helpfulness: Every major section must answer a decision question or remove uncertainty.
content_quality.duplication: Keep generic course explanation at the pillar; university-specific data belongs on the programme page.
content_quality.editorial_voice: Clear, neutral, student-first, non-hype, simple language.

mobile_ux.top_area: Course name + one-line value proposition + key facts + sticky/compact table of contents.
mobile_ux.toc: Collapsible horizontal/vertical navigation; do not consume the first screen with a giant table of contents.
mobile_ux.tables: Convert wide fee/comparison tables into stacked cards or controlled horizontal scrolling with the first identifying column sticky.
mobile_ux.directory: University cards should remain scannable with fee, duration, mode and CTA visible without opening a huge card.
mobile_ux.cta: Use restrained CTAs: View course details, Compare, Check admission. Avoid repeated popups.
mobile_ux.performance: Lazy-load below-fold images; avoid large hero assets; reserve dimensions to prevent layout shift.

next_step_pattern.purpose: After major educational sections, provide one relevant next action rather than a generic CTA.

examples.next_step: Explore universities offering your preferred specialisation
View the exact university admission process

next_step_pattern.rule: These are contextual navigation aids, not aggressive lead-generation blocks.

implementation_constraints: Do not change existing university-course URLs.
Do not delete existing verified university-course data.
Do not duplicate all university-course content into the pillar.
Do not generate 100+ thin pages from keyword permutations.
Do not create separate pages solely for each section anchor.
Do not make claims of 'best' without transparent criteria.
Do not add fake rankings, salaries, placement percentages or recognition claims.
Do not add competitor brand names repeatedly just to capture search traffic.
Do not use AI-generated filler to increase word count.

required_before_phase_5: All nine main course hubs exist and are indexable.
Each hub has unique course-specific content.
Each hub links to all currently available relevant university-course pages.
Every university-course page links back to its parent hub.
No keyword-permutation duplicate pages were created.
Core Web Vitals are not materially degraded.
All dynamic claims have source/verification handling.
FAQ content is visible and valid for FAQ schema.
No existing good content was deleted.

lovable_prompt:
PHASE 4 — MAIN COURSE PILLAR PAGES ONLY

Implement the attached Phase 4 JSON.

Build/upgrade the nine main course pillar pages:
Online MBA, Online MCA, Online BBA, Online BCA, Online BCom, Online BA, Online MA, Online M.Sc. and Online MCom.

IMPORTANT:
1. Preserve all existing good content, routes, components, university-course pages and comparison pages.
2. Do not rebuild the whole website.
3. Do not modify existing university-course URLs.
4. Do not copy all university-course content into the pillar.
5. Make each pillar the broad informational hub and the university-course pages the exact programme pages.
6. Implement the section structure, original content framework, SEO contract, internal-linking architecture and mobile UX from this JSON.
7. Build the university directory dynamically from existing verified programme data.
8. Every directory card must link to the exact canonical university-course page.
9. Every university-course page must link back to its parent course hub.
10. Use official sources for dynamic facts and show last verified dates.
11. Do not invent fees, eligibility, recognition, rankings, placements, salaries or curriculum.
12. Do not create thin keyword-permutation pages.
13. Use contextual 'Next step' navigation after major sections.
14. Keep the comparison experience separate; only link to it from the pillar.
15. Keep desktop and mobile layouts clean; no horizontal overflow at common mobile widths.
16. Keep images lightweight and avoid a giant hero that pushes useful content below the fold.
17. Preserve existing analytics, routing, SEO infrastructure and working functionality.

After implementation, provide:
- files/components changed
- pages created/updated
- sections implemented per course
- university links verified
- internal-link audit
- SEO audit
- mobile QA
- content duplication issues found
- existing content intentionally preserved
- anything requiring manual review

This is PHASE 4 ONLY. Do not implement Phase 5.
